The test explicitly exercises vertex index 0 (a boundary for vertex indices) and a self-loop (0->0), which represents an edge/boundary scenario rather than only mid-range values.

The test is self-contained, follows Arrange-Act-Assert (Given-When-Then) and there is no duplicated setup across multiple tests in the visible code; no helper extraction is strictly required for this single case.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: The method is short (well under 20-30 lines) and contains no loops or complex conditionals—simple linear Arrange-Act-Assert flow.

The test contains multiple specific assertions verifying several properties of the transposed graph (instance identity, vertex count, existence of self-loop, adjacency properties), not just a superficial null check.
No @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out @Test methods are present; the test is active and runnable.
The class Javadoc explicitly references 'REQ-001', providing traceability to a requirement for the tests in this class.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: The test method includes an explicit timeout annotation (@Test(timeout = 4000)), which is an explicit performance-related assertion allowed by the decision rules.
The test method name 'test7' is generic and does not describe the scenario or expected outcome despite the internal Given-When-Then comments; it does not follow descriptive naming conventions.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: The test class uses EvoSuite/EvoRunner and the test method is named 'test7', which are indicators of generated tests (auto-generated naming and test runner scaffolding), suggesting heavy code generation signatures.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The method includes explicit Given-When-Then comments and exercises a meaningful scenario (transposing a graph with a self-loop), indicating thoughtful test design rather than ad-hoc one-liners.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test interacts only with public APIs of Grafo and does not access private fields or use reflection; it asserts observable behavior rather than internal implementation details.
Assertions are specific (assertEquals, assertTrue, assertNotNull, assertNotSame) and several include descriptive failure messages, improving diagnosability.
The test includes minimal, useful Given-When-Then inline comments and class-level Javadoc; there is no excessive or commented-out code.
No sources of non-determinism (randomness, current time, Thread.sleep) are used in the method; inputs are fixed and deterministic.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test creates local Grafo instances and does not persist data, modify static variables, or leave resources open; no cleanup is necessary for local-only state.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: The class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class), enabling categorization and selective execution.
